/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 23 July 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2725 (10)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4198 (84)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2064 (-56)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1702 (-13)
Baltic Handysize Index: 906 (1)
CAPESIZE
The market extended its gains today, with firmer sentiment evident across both the Pacific and Atlantic basins as improving confidence continued to support rates. The BCI 182 5TC index increased by $764 to $38,072, with the C5 index rising by 0.340 to $12.115, while C3 advanced by 0.690 to $34.135. In the Pacific, the market maintained a firm tone despite only two major C5 miners being active. Early in the session, an operator was bidding $11.90, with rumours circulating that $12.00 had been paid. One miner was reportedly bidding $11.80 against offers around $12.20, reflecting owners’ continued confidence and a narrowing gap between bids and achievable levels. The Atlantic also remained firm, with conditions continuing to improve on South Brazil and West Africa to China business. Reports emerged that $33.75 had been concluded late yesterday for 19/25 August dates. Today, bids opened around $33.50 before improving to $34.00, while offers for end-August laycan were heard in the mid-to-upper $34s. Following the index, market talk suggested that $34.30 had been paid, reinforcing the positive sentiment. Brent crude remained elevated after briefly approaching $98 per barrel, with renewed concerns over potential disruptions to both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb keeping bunker price risk firmly in focus.
PANAMAX
Market sentiment remained negative in both basins today, although reported trading activity increased. Rates came under further pressure with levels concluded below previous fixtures, resulting in the P5TC declining by $509 to $18,574. In the Atlantic some brokers reported a thinning cargo list, while Owners with prompt tonnage continued to reduce offers in an effort to secure employment. Market participants noted that Charterers remain content to sit back and assess market direction, as well as the potential for further rate softening, before re-engaging. Although some prompt tonnage has reportedly been absorbed, a meaningful increase in cargo volume will be required before the market can establish a more convincing floor. The Pacific remained under pressure, with market fundamentals said to be increasingly imbalanced as vessel supply continues to grow against a backdrop of limited fresh enquiry. Demand from both the North Pacific and East Coast Australia has also lost momentum, adding to the negative sentiment. Market sources indicated that Charterers continue to test levels below those of recently concluded fixtures as rates trend lower. Indonesia has also weakened with scarce coal enquiry forcing Owners to compete more aggressively for available business.

Atlantic
The Crimson Empress (82,250 2014) open Bilbao 26 July was said to have been placed on subjects for a North Coast South America round between $21,250 - $21,500 to Glencore. Both the BH Strive (82,107 2026) open New Orleans 5/9 August and the Aurora Borealis (82,315 2023) open Gibraltar 30 July were said to have been placed on subjects for a trans Atlantic round. The Navios Alegria (84,852 2016) open Gibraltar 28/30 July was also said to have been placed on subjects for a trip via Colombia to Taiwan around $33,000 and the Maple Well (82,253 2025) open Abidjan 1/4 Aug was said to have fixed for a fronthaul trip via the North Coast or East Coast South America to Cofco, although a rate did not surface.

Pacific
The Samatan (77,154 2015) was reported as placed on subjects from Hong Kong 25 July for a trip via Indonesia to SE Asia, while the scrubber fitted Basic Faith (82,029 2025) open Bahodopi 29 July was understood to have also been placed on subjects. The Chinook (93,266 2012), also open Bahodopi 26/28 July, was said to be on subjects at $17,500 to Five Ocean for a trip with coal loading Indonesia to South Korea. Further north, the scrubber fitted XH Deep Cover (83,070 2024) open Dafeng 23/25 July was reported to have been placed on subjects, but no other details surfaced. The scrubber fitted Gouverneur (82,038 2026) was placed on subjects for an East Coast Australia round at $17,000. The Shine Pearl (82,427 2024) was placed on subjects basis delivery Hong Kong 26/27 July for an East Coast Australia to India trip with coal at $19,000 to LSS. Elsewhere, the Alcor (81,118 2015) Cam Pha 29/30 July fixed for a West Coast Australia round. The VitaOcean (82,250 2013) Jingtang 30 July/5 August was reported to have been placed on subjects with LSS for an Australia to India trip at $16,000, while the Ocean Anna (82,206 2011) open CJK 30 July was placed on subjects by Cobelfret for a trip via Bunbury to Iceland.
SUPRAMAX
A dissappointing day with mostly red on the indices as the week draws to a close. Again the North American market was the hardest hit as supply outweighs demand and Charterers take advantage of the weaker sentiment. The Mediterranean continues to show the most resistance driven by demand in the East Med and the Black Sea, whilst the Continent appeared to succumb to a lack of scrap demand. In the South rates are flatter but the bid/offer is widening, so it remains to be seen who blinks first. In Asia we saw a small reduction in rates as competition from the declining Panamax market had a knock on affect on what has been a fairly well balanced market until now. Period rates are yet to reflect any decline with a 60,000-dwt JMU fixed for short period delivery Vietnam at $22,750. The 11TC dropped another $162 down to $21,512.
HANDYSIZE
The Handy market saw another mixed day,with sentiment largely shaped by positional factors. Across the Continent and Mediterranean changes were minimal and the market appeared balanced, with rates recorded a tick higher than last done. The South Atlantic and US Gulf remained on a softer note as the tonnage list continued to lengthen. On the Asian side, fixing information was limited, but the market maintained a firm tone. Brokers reported that tonnage had begun to clear out in Southeast Asia and the North Pacific, prompting charterers to raise their bids. Reflecting these regional variations, the 7TC average improved by $20 to close at $16,315.

Atlantic
A 40,000-dwt was heard fixed for a trip delivery West Africa 23–28 July via EC South America to the Continent at $15,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
The Frida Bulker (40,161 2023) was reported fixed via West Australia to Japan at $22,000, while the Melody Selmer (37,452 2013) open Singapore was fixed for an Australia round trip at $18,000, although further details were not disclosed. A 35,000-dwt was also heard fixed from Yeosu 26–28 July for a trip via EC India with redelivery Singapore at $12,000, again further details were lacking.

ai_analysis.summary: 24Jul26 dry bulk market分化明显,cape强支撑领涨(BCI+84),但panamax和supramax继续承压下跌。cape5TC已至$38,072,大西洋c3冲高$34.135,太平洋c5站稳$12.0;panamax双端走弱p5TC跌$509;handysize局部回暖。ffacape远期曲线强势,pmx曲线平稳,smx平淡。宏观关注伊朗局势及中东油运风险对bunker成本影响。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: cape短期维持强势,c3c5价差交易机会;pmx aug/dec 26 strip 18,900-19,050可关注;smx aug 18,700-18,900区间窄幅整理缺乏方向。handysize亚洲航线hs5/6/7上涨值得跟踪。关注cape period bid 35,000 35,200测试。
